11| /-!
12| # Uniformly almost periodic functions
13| -/
14| 
15| variable {E F : Set ℝ} {C D ε δ t l : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → ℂ}
16| 
17| variable (E l) in
18| /-- A set `E` of reals is **relatively dense with respect to `l`** if every (closed-open) interval
19| of length `l` contains an element of `E`. -/
20| def IsRelDenseWith : Prop := ∀ x, ∃ y ∈ Set.Ico 0 l, x + y ∈ E
21| 
22| lemma IsRelDenseWith.subset (hEF : E ⊆ F) : IsRelDenseWith E l → IsRelDenseWith F l :=
23|   forall_imp fun _x ↦ .imp fun _l ↦ .imp_right <| @hEF _
24| 
25| lemma IsRelDenseWith.pos (hE : IsRelDenseWith E l) : 0 < l := by
26|   obtain ⟨y, ⟨hy₀, hyl⟩, _⟩ := hE 0; exact hy₀.trans_lt hyl
27| 
28| variable (E) in
29| /-- A set `E` of reals is **relatively dense** if it is relatively dense with respect to some `l`.
30| -/
31| def IsRelDense : Prop := ∃ l, IsRelDenseWith E l
32| 
33| lemma IsRelDense.subset (hEF : E ⊆ F) : IsRelDense E → IsRelDense F := .imp fun _ ↦ .subset hEF
34| 
35| variable (ε t f) in
36| /-- A real number `t` is an **`ε`, L∞-almost period** of a function `f : ℝ \r ℝ` if
37| `‖f - τ t f‖_∞ ≤ ε`. -/
38| def IsLinftyAP : Prop := ∀ x, ‖f (x + t) - f x‖ ≤ ε
39| 
40| lemma IsLinftyAP.mul_fun (hfbdd : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hgbdd : ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ D)
41|     (hf : IsLinftyAP ε t f) (hg : IsLinftyAP δ t g) : IsLinftyAP (D * ε + C * δ) t (f * g) := by
42|   rintro x
43|   have := hf x
44|   have := hg x
45|   have := hfbdd (x + t)
46|   have := hgbdd x
47|   calc
48|         ‖f (x + t) * g (x + t) - f x * g x‖
49|     _ = ‖g x * (f (x + t) - f x) + f (x + t) * (g (x + t) - g x)‖ := by ring_nf
50|     _ ≤ ‖g x * (f (x + t) - f x)‖ + ‖f (x + t) * (g (x + t) - g x)‖ := norm_add_le ..
51|     _ = ‖g x‖ * ‖f (x + t) - f x‖ + ‖f (x + t)‖ * ‖g (x + t) - g x‖ := by simp
52|     _ ≤ D * ε + C * δ := by gcongr <;> exact (norm_nonneg _).trans ‹_›
53| 
54| variable (f) in
55| /-- A function `f : ℝ → ℂ` is **uniformly almost periodic** if its set of `ε`, L∞-almost period is
56| relatively dense for all `ε > 0`. -/
57| def IsUnifAlmostPeriodic : Prop := ∀ ⦃ε⦄, 0 < ε → IsRelDense {t | IsLinftyAP ε t f}
58| 
59| /-- Any uniformly almost periodic function is uniformly continuous. -/
60| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.uniformContinuous (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f) :
61|     UniformContinuous f := sorry
62| 
63| /-- Any uniformly almost periodic function is bounded. -/
64| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.exists_forall_le (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f) : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C :=
65|   sorry
66| 
67| /-- The intersection of the almost periods of two uniformly almost periodic functions is relatively
68| dense. -/
69| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.isRelDense_inter (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f)
70|     (hg : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic g) (hε : 0 < ε) :
71|     IsRelDense {t | IsLinftyAP ε t f ∧ IsLinftyAP ε t g} := sorry
72| 
73| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.mul (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f) (hg : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic g) :
74|     IsUnifAlmostPeriodic (f * g) := by
75|   rintro ε hε
76|   obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hf.exists_forall_le
77|   obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hg.exists_forall_le

11| /-!
12| # Uniformly almost periodic functions
13| -/
14| 
15| variable {E F : Set ℝ} {C D ε δ t l : ℝ} {f g : ℝ → ℂ}
16| 
17| variable (E l) in
18| /-- A set `E` of reals is **relatively dense with respect to `l`** if every (closed-open) interval
19| of length `l` contains an element of `E`. -/
20| def IsRelDenseWith : Prop := ∀ x, ∃ y ∈ Set.Ico 0 l, x + y ∈ E
21| 
22| lemma IsRelDenseWith.subset (hEF : E ⊆ F) : IsRelDenseWith E l → IsRelDenseWith F l :=
23|   forall_imp fun _x ↦ .imp fun _l ↦ .imp_right <| @hEF _
24| 
25| lemma IsRelDenseWith.pos (hE : IsRelDenseWith E l) : 0 < l := by
26|   obtain ⟨y, ⟨hy₀, hyl⟩, _⟩ := hE 0; exact hy₀.trans_lt hyl
27| 
28| variable (E) in
29| /-- A set `E` of reals is **relatively dense** if it is relatively dense with respect to some `l`.
30| -/
31| def IsRelDense : Prop := ∃ l, IsRelDenseWith E l
32| 
33| lemma IsRelDense.subset (hEF : E ⊆ F) : IsRelDense E → IsRelDense F := .imp fun _ ↦ .subset hEF
34| 
35| variable (ε t f) in
36| /-- A real number `t` is an **`ε`, L∞-almost period** of a function `f : ℝ \r ℝ` if
37| `‖f - τ t f‖_∞ ≤ ε`. -/
38| def IsLinftyAP : Prop := ∀ x, ‖f (x + t) - f x‖ ≤ ε
39| 
40| lemma IsLinftyAP.mul_fun (hfbdd : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C) (hgbdd : ∀ x, ‖g x‖ ≤ D)
41|     (hf : IsLinftyAP ε t f) (hg : IsLinftyAP δ t g) : IsLinftyAP (D * ε + C * δ) t (f * g) := by
42|   rintro x
43|   have := hf x
44|   have := hg x
45|   have := hfbdd (x + t)
46|   have := hgbdd x
47|   calc
48|         ‖f (x + t) * g (x + t) - f x * g x‖
49|     _ = ‖g x * (f (x + t) - f x) + f (x + t) * (g (x + t) - g x)‖ := by ring_nf
50|     _ ≤ ‖g x * (f (x + t) - f x)‖ + ‖f (x + t) * (g (x + t) - g x)‖ := norm_add_le ..
51|     _ = ‖g x‖ * ‖f (x + t) - f x‖ + ‖f (x + t)‖ * ‖g (x + t) - g x‖ := by simp
52|     _ ≤ D * ε + C * δ := by gcongr <;> exact (norm_nonneg _).trans ‹_›
53| 
54| variable (f) in
55| /-- A function `f : ℝ → ℂ` is **uniformly almost periodic** if its set of `ε`, L∞-almost period is
56| relatively dense for all `ε > 0`. -/
57| def IsUnifAlmostPeriodic : Prop := ∀ ⦃ε⦄, 0 < ε → IsRelDense {t | IsLinftyAP ε t f}
58| 
59| /-- Any uniformly almost periodic function is uniformly continuous. -/
60| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.uniformContinuous (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f) :
61|     UniformContinuous f := sorry
62| 
63| /-- Any uniformly almost periodic function is bounded. -/
64| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.exists_forall_le (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f) : ∃ C, ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ C :=
65|   sorry
66| 
67| /-- The intersection of the almost periods of two uniformly almost periodic functions is relatively
68| dense. -/
69| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.isRelDense_inter (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f)
70|     (hg : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic g) (hε : 0 < ε) :
71|     IsRelDense {t | IsLinftyAP ε t f ∧ IsLinftyAP ε t g} := sorry
72| 
73| lemma IsUnifAlmostPeriodic.mul (hf : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic f) (hg : IsUnifAlmostPeriodic g) :
74|     IsUnifAlmostPeriodic (f * g) := by
75|   rintro ε hε
76|   obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hf.exists_forall_le
77|   obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := hg.exists_forall_le
78|   have hC₀ : 0 ≤ C := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hC 0)

9| /-! # Spec Theorem for `EdwardsPoint::to_montgomery`
10| 
11| Specification and proof for `EdwardsPoint::to_montgomery`.
12| 
13| This function converts an EdwardsPoint from the twisted Edwards curve to the
14| corresponding MontgomeryPoint (only the u-coordinate) on the Montgomery curve, using the birational map
15| u = (1+y)/(1-y) = (Z+Y)/(Z-Y).
16| 
17| **Source**: curve25519-dalek/src/edwards.rs
18| 
19| ## TODO
20| - Complete proof
21| -/
22| 
23| open Aeneas.Std Result
24| namespace curve25519_dalek.edwards.EdwardsPoint
25| 
26| /-
27| natural language description:
28| 
29| • Converts an EdwardsPoint from extended twisted Edwards coordinates (X, Y, Z, T)
30| to a MontgomeryPoint (u-coordinate only), using the birational map:
31|   - u ≡ (1+y)/(1-y) ≡ (Z+Y)/(Z-Y) (mod p)
32| 
33| • Special case: when Y = Z (affine y = 1, the identity point on Edwards curve),
34|   the denominator is zero. Since 0.invert() = 0 in this implementation,
35|   this yields u = 0.
36| 
37| • The output u is represented as an U8x32 array (a type alias for MontgomeryPoint)
38| 
39| natural language specs:
40| 
41| • The function always succeeds (no panic)

9| /-!
10| # VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺²
11| 
12| In the literature it is known that every convex set in ℝ² has VC dimension at most 3,
13| and there exists a convex set in ℝ³ with infinite VC dimension (even more strongly,
14| which shatters an infinite set).
15| 
16| This file proves that every convex set in ℝⁿ has finite VCₙ dimension, constructs a convex set in
17| ℝⁿ⁺² with infinite VCₙ dimension (even more strongly, which n-shatters an infinite set),
18| and conjectures that every convex set in ℝⁿ⁺¹ has finite VCₙ dimension.
19| -/

31|       ∀ i s, x i + y s ∈ C ↔ i ∈ s := sorry

9| /-!
10| # VCₙ dimension of convex sets in ℝⁿ⁺¹, ℝⁿ⁺²
11| 
12| In the literature it is known that every convex set in ℝ² has VC dimension at most 3,
13| and there exists a convex set in ℝ³ with infinite VC dimension (even more strongly,
14| which shatters an infinite set).
15| 
16| This file proves that every convex set in ℝⁿ has finite VCₙ dimension, constructs a convex set in
17| ℝⁿ⁺² with infinite VCₙ dimension (even more strongly, which n-shatters an infinite set),
18| and conjectures that every convex set in ℝⁿ⁺¹ has finite VCₙ dimension.
19| -/

23| /-- Every convex set in ℝ² has VC dimension at most 3. -/
24| lemma vc_lt_four_of_convex_r2 {C : Set (Fin 2 → ℝ)} (hC : Convex ℝ C)
25|     {x : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → ℝ} {y : Set (Fin 4) → Fin 2 → ℝ}
26|     (hxy : ∀ i s, x i + y s ∈ C ↔ i ∈ s) : False := sorry

30|     ∃ (C : Set (Fin 3 → ℝ)) (hC : Convex ℝ C) (x : ℕ → Fin 3 → ℝ) (y : Set ℕ → Fin 3 → ℝ),
31|       ∀ i s, x i + y s ∈ C ↔ i ∈ s := sorry
